samples.summary: `isCredentialRejected` misses AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL — the single most likely per-slot bad-secret case still refuses to fail over
samples.evidence: `isCredentialRejected` returns `err.code === "AUTH_REJECTED"` as soon as `err.code` is truthy (ask.mjs:602). But `classifyInfraError` (redact.mjs:390) tests `MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL_RE` BEFORE the status branch, so a slot whose token has a stray space/newline — the exact incident redact.mjs's header documents — is classified `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL`, not `AUTH_REJECTED`, even when it arrives with a 401. The `code` branch short-circuits the 401/403 status fallback, so `nextCredential` returns null and the run dies on that slot with the other pool credentials unused. That is precisely the outage class this change claims to fix, and it is per-slot (a malformed secret in one env var), so the other pool members are healthy and failover would work.

samples.summary: Widening SESSION_LIMIT_RE to daily/monthly makes short-window rate limits retire pool credentials instead of backing off
samples.evidence: `SESSION_LIMIT_RE = /\b(?:session|usage|weekly|daily|monthly)\s+limit\b/i` now drives three decisions at once: `retryable = false` (ask.mjs:385), `code = USAGE_LIMIT` (redact.mjs:393) and failover/retire via `isAccountLimit` → `pool.advance` (ask.mjs:639-640). Upstream 429 prose such as "you have exceeded your daily limit of requests" is a short-window rate limit that clears in seconds, but it now matches: the error becomes permanently non-retryable and each occurrence RETIRES a credential. With the panel running lenses concurrently, a burst of such 429s can retire every slot in one round and turn a transient rate limit into a `pool-exhausted` failure for the whole job. `weekly`/`monthly` are safe; `daily` is the one that overlaps normal rate-limit phrasing.

samples.summary: Replacing the smoke test's literal quota patterns with SESSION_LIMIT_RE narrows them: plural/punctuated forms no longer match
samples.evidence: The removed patterns were unanchored substrings (`/session limit/i`, `/usage limit/i`), so they matched "usage limits exceeded", "session limit-reached" etc. `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` ends in `limit\b`, which does NOT match "limits" (no boundary between `t` and `s`) and requires `\s+` between the words, so "usage limits exceeded" and "session-limit" now fall through QUOTA. If no other QUOTA pattern (`quota`, `429`, `rate limit`) also matches, `classifyFailure` returns "unknown" and the script exits 1 — the exact quota-read-as-auth misdiagnosis auth-smoke.mjs's header (lines 26-30) says is the worst thing a pre-arm check can do.

samples.summary: Any 403 is treated as a per-credential refusal, including account/org-wide policy refusals that will drain the whole pool
samples.evidence: `return status === 401 || status === 403;` (and `AUTH_REJECTED` from redact.mjs:400, which also collapses 401 and 403). A 403 is frequently a policy/permission refusal that is identical for every credential (model not enabled for the org, region block). Under the new rule each such failure retires a slot, so `askStructured`'s `for(;;)` loop walks and retires the entire pool, after which every later call in the process throws the generic `pool-exhausted` error and the actionable 403 diagnosis is lost. 401 has the per-secret property the docblock argues for; 403 does not necessarily.

samples.summary: An all-bad or single-credential pool now reports the generic "was retired" message instead of the actionable auth error for every subsequent call
samples.evidence: With a pool of one (or once every slot is refused), the first 401 now retires the sole slot via `nextCredential`. The original error is rethrown for that call, but every LATER `askStructured` call in the process hits `pool.isExhausted()` (ask.mjs:691) and throws `pool-exhausted: every credential in the pool (N) was retired`, which names neither a closed window nor a refused secret. Before this change a 401 never retired anything, so each lens surfaced the real `[AUTH_REJECTED]` reason. The panel's per-lens infra summaries therefore degrade to a non-diagnostic message for the common single-token setup.

samples.summary: metrics.mjs still carries its own un-widened copy of the session/usage regex the change just centralised
samples.evidence: `const sessionLimited = outcome.code ? outcome.code === "USAGE_LIMIT" : /\b(?:session|usage)\s+limit\b/i.test(detail);` — the prose fallback (used for persisted, pre-vocabulary records, per the comment above it) was not widened with `weekly|daily|monthly` and was not switched to the now-exported `SESSION_LIMIT_RE`. A replayed/persisted record carrying "weekly limit" prose without a `code` renders the wrong advice ("a human should take a look" instead of "wait for the window to reset") — the same drift the redact.mjs docblock says this change exists to eliminate.

samples.summary: No test covers failover for a 401 that classifyResult labels AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL
samples.evidence: The new tests construct `{ kind: "api-error", code: "AUTH_REJECTED", status: 401 }` by hand and never drive a realistic malformed-credential message (redact.test.mjs's INCIDENT string) through `classifyResult` → `isCredentialRejected` → `nextCredential`. That end-to-end path is the one that silently returns null (see the AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL finding), so nothing in the suite would catch it.

finding.summary: `isCredentialRejected` misses AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL — the single most likely per-slot bad-secret case still refuses to fail over
finding.evidence: `isCredentialRejected` returns `err.code === "AUTH_REJECTED"` as soon as `err.code` is truthy (ask.mjs:602). But `classifyInfraError` (redact.mjs:390) tests `MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL_RE` BEFORE the status branch, so a slot whose token has a stray space/newline — the exact incident redact.mjs's header documents — is classified `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL`, not `AUTH_REJECTED`, even when it arrives with a 401. verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `isCredentialRejected` (scripts/agent/ask.mjs:600-605) short-circuits on `err.code` at line 602 and only accepts `AUTH_REJECTED`. `classifyInfraError` (scripts/agent/redact.mjs:382-403) tests `MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL_RE` at line 390 BEFORE the `NO_RESPONSE`/`401||403` branches (397-400), so a slot whose token contains an invalid header character classifies as `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL` (with or without a status). `runSession` stamps `err.kind = "api-error"` and `err.code = c.code` (ask.mjs:786-788) via classifyResult's api-error branch (ask.mjs:378-386), so the failover loop sees a truthy non-`AUTH_REJECTED` code: `nextCredential` returns null (ask.mjs:639) and the loop rethrows (ask.mjs:717-718), killing the run while the other pool credentials are untouched. This is per-slot and is the exact incident documented at redact.mjs:3-14 (a token rotated "with a stray space in it"). I checked for a guard elsewhere: `readPoolSlots` only `.trim()`s (token-pool.mjs:57), which strips leading/trailing whitespace but not the internal space of the documented incident, and `createTokenPool` performs no token validation (token-pool.mjs:126-137) — so `already-guarded` does not apply. Tests (ask.test.mjs:267-278) and the task doc's acceptance criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260815-agent-pool-failover-todo.md:45,56) cover only 401/403, confirming the malformed case is unhandled rather than deliberately re-routed. Real, reachable, and in the correctness lane (incomplete condition → job fails with healthy failover targets unused).

finding.summary: Widening SESSION_LIMIT_RE to daily/monthly makes short-window rate limits retire pool credentials instead of backing off
finding.evidence: `SESSION_LIMIT_RE = /\b(?:session|usage|weekly|daily|monthly)\s+limit\b/i` now drives three decisions at once: `retryable = false` (ask.mjs:385), `code = USAGE_LIMIT` (redact.mjs:393) and failover/retire via `isAccountLimit` → `pool.advance` (ask.mjs:639-640). Upstream 429 prose such as "you have exceeded your daily limit of requests" is a short-window rate limit that clears in seconds, but it now matches: the error becomes permanently non-retryable and each occurrence RETIRES a credential. With the panel running lenses concurrently, a burst of such 429s can retire every slot in one round and turn a transient rate limit into a `pool-exhausted` failure for the whole job. `weekly`/`monthly` are safe; `daily` is the one that overlaps normal rate-limit phrasing.

verdict.reason: The regex and its three consumers are present as quoted (redact.mjs:305, redact.mjs:393, ask.mjs:385, ask.mjs:570, ask.mjs:638-641), but the harm mechanism the finding rests on does not hold. (a) The claimed "burst of 429s retires every slot in one round -> pool-exhausted for the whole job" is blocked by the idempotence guard in token-pool.mjs:171: advance() is a no-op unless the reporter's dead token is the pool's CURRENT token, and nextCredential always passes the failing session's own token (ask.mjs:640). Concurrent lenses hitting one closed window retire exactly one slot; token-pool.test.mjs:206-216 pins this. Draining the pool requires every credential to be tried and to individually report a limit. (b) The premise that matching text denotes a limit "that clears in seconds" contradicts the text matched: the pattern requires literal adjacency to " limit" (redact.mjs:305), so it fires only on prose asserting a day-scale window was exhausted -- including the reviewer's own example "exceeded your daily limit of requests", which resets at a day boundary, not in seconds. For such an error, failover is the correct response and backoff is not; the pre-change "retryable" path was only withRetry's 2 retries at baseMs 2000 (ask.mjs:405-417), i.e. ~6s, which would not clear a daily window either. (c) It is not a permanent job-wide failure while slots remain: askStructured's loop continues on the next credential (ask.mjs:708-721), and pool-exhausted (ask.mjs:691-698) fires only after isExhausted(). No other consumer aborts on a single USAGE_LIMIT. The behavior is also pinned intentionally at redact.test.mjs:168.
